events.title: Unix language before C created
events.summary: Around 1969, Ken Thompson created the B language at Bell Labs — a minimal stepping stone between BCPL and C for early Unix development.
events.about: B was a small language for writing Unix kernel code and utilities on memory-limited minicomputers. Thompson built its compiler after finding FORTRAN too bulky for the hardware. Dennis Ritchie then added data types and turned B into C — the language that still underpins operating systems worldwide.

narrative.whyChosen: Unix needed a lightweight language for systems work; B was the experiment that proved the approach before C added proper types.
narrative.whyImportant: B established the BCPL → B → C lineage that defines how operating systems and device drivers are still written.
narrative.problemSolved: The PDP-7 had very little memory, and existing languages were too large to compile or run on the new Unix hardware.

sources.title: Ritchie — The Development of the C Language (B created 1969–70)
